rationale: Both are correct and thread-safe, with mutex-guarded counters updated after delegating to the wrapped reader or writer. B avoids duplication through composition: readWriteCounter simply embeds a readCounter and a writeCounter over the same ReadWriter, so the counting logic exists in exactly one place. A re-implements all four methods a second time for readWriteCounter with separate fields. Its stated reason, that a single mutex keeps ReadCount and WriteCount consistent with each other, adds little because the two counts are read by separate calls anyway. A's struct field alignment is also not gofmt-clean. B's constructor uses type assertions on its own constructors where direct struct literals would be simpler, which is a small wart. Overall B is the more idiomatic, DRY design.
